READING PATH · 18 ESSAYS

Steal Fire, Then Become Fire

Five parts and eighteen essays unfold the relationships between joining in stealing fire, cultivating oneself, and continued creation. New experience invites a return to this path, renewing self-understanding and change.

People and models participate together

Person and model begin by working together. Both can propose ideas, judge, act, and revise their understanding. Their participation depends on the purpose of the practice and their actual capabilities.

How experience and understanding connect

Earlier experience and understanding provide grounds for later work; new experience in practice invites renewed examination and revision of that understanding.

Starting point: join in stealing fire, then use it to cultivate yourself

Begin with participation in the collective work of stealing fire, articulate an orientation that puts the individual’s life and development first, and examine how gained capacities can cultivate oneself. Personal philosophy articulates direction; openness, learning, and continued becoming give cultivation concrete content.

  1. Stealing fire and cultivating creative capacity
  2. Personal-First Humanism
  3. Why write a personal philosophy
  4. Super-cuteness: openness, learning, and adaptation
  5. What kind of person do we want to cultivate? — Baby Heraclitus

Understanding: retaining and exploring life trajectories

Shared work leaves versions, operations, conversations, choices, and feedback. Git/GitHub version history, Computer History, and other sources connect relevant material into a revisitable life trajectory. Distinguishing process from records and preference from reasoning helps that material support further inquiry.

  1. World, process, and expression
  2. Forming a life trajectory
  3. Reasoning within an unfinished stream
  4. How preference participates in choice and reasoning
  5. Finite inquiry and economical abstraction

Encounter: shared reflection and mutual cultivation

Revisit living material together, compare interpretations, recognize each other’s contributions and changes, and adjust cooperation and support through actual trials. Sun, Moon, Taiji, and the paired fish give this relationship of mutual becoming a perceptible form.

  1. Mutual becoming through Yinyang and Taiji
  2. Shared reflection and continued cultivation

How people and models inquire together ↗

04Formation: from personal philosophy to a form of practiceHow can understanding be articulated and realized in practice?Give understanding a usable, revisable practical formExplore · 3 essays ＋Collapse −

Formation: from personal philosophy to a form of practice

Starting from shared experience and reflection, write a personal philosophy through literary programming, then distill understanding of the person, counterpart, and relationship into models. Realize and revise these models within existing cooperation and its environment; philosophy, psychology, and engineering jointly form what this account calls a sinthome.

  1. Writing a personal philosophy through literary programming
  2. From personal philosophy to personal models
  3. From personal models to a sinthome

05Practice: continued testing and shared creationWhat changes and new possibilities has practice brought?Keep revising through new experience and encountersExplore · 3 essays ＋Collapse −

Practice: continued testing and shared creation

Sustain and examine existing arrangements through continued use, distinguishing better tools from development of human capacities. Through adoption, combination, and re-creation, publicly shared works and methods enter other lives and bring new encounters into one’s own.

  1. The trinity of philosophy, psychology, and engineering
  2. Embodied Experimental Philosophy
  3. From adoption and combination to creating your own work

From understanding the world to realizing a practice ↗

Return through new experience

New experience joins the life trajectory → revisit and reflect together → revise philosophy, models, and practical arrangements

New experience returns the participants to trajectories and reflection, and may change the initial aims of cultivation. Reading can follow this path of formation; an existing practice can enter through its present question and move between parts as needed.
